thread:
olivia: Quick sync — two APAC pilots asked for a low-latency edge routing option + stronger tenant isolation after a competitor announcement. Do we treat this as parity or a targeted differentiator?

raj: Can you paste the asks?

olivia: Short version: 1) ~50ms p50 target for APAC regions for small chat workloads, 2) option to keep request metadata off-host (customer-managed KV), 3) SLA language for pilot accounts. Both are small-medium fintechs.

tess: engineering quick thought: we can ship a shim (regional routing + aggressive prefix caching) in 2 sprints. True private-edge with VPC + KMS takes months.

kai: From sales: both accounts are willing to sign pilot terms if we promise an APAC-friendly latency story. One mentions competitor offering a hosted-edge product.

mike: Ops flag: shim increases cache complexity and could mask cold-start issues. We'd need a strict rollout gating to avoid SLO regression elsewhere.

sam: Product trade: do we carve this as "edge-fastlane" (narrow capability, paid add-on) or fold into Redwood Private roadmap?

olivia: Proposal A: quick shim as paid pilot feature + strict rollout + canary tenants. Launch criteria: p50 < 60ms APAC chat tokens, p99 < 250ms, no increase in global error budget > 1% for 24h after rollout, documented fallback to regional hosted models.

Proposal B: push to Private roadmap (longer) with customer-managed KV and VPC — better long-term differentiator but delayed.

raj: If we go A, we should also instrument economic signal (tokens saved per request via caching) and capture a simple cost uplift model for customers. Sales won't pay unless it's predictable.

tess: Implementation notes for A: route matching rule by tenant tag, region-local KV prefix cache, optional metadata suppression header X-Redwood-No-Meta. We'll need a small auth shim and a flag in the routing table. I can scope a spike this week.

mike: Rollout plan: canary on 1 pilot tenant -> 3 pilot tenants -> open pilot. We'll need a rollback-on-latency spike automation and observability dashboard (per-tenant latency + cache hit rate).

kai: Can we commit to SLA language for pilot? Sales asks specific uptime + latency refund language. For pilot, keep it "commercially reasonable" but include our monitoring thresholds.

sam: Customer success asks: acceptance criteria from customers: sample traffic, SLO validation run for 72h, and a short security checklist (no PII in logs).

eval-bot: Quick eval note: competitor's hosted-edge appears to tradeoff consistency for p50 gains; their p99 is often worse. That suggests a niche differentiator for us if we optimize for tail.

olivia: Next steps: tess does spike & perf estimate by Thu, mike drafts rollout + rollback automation by Fri, raj & kai draft pilot commercial terms and launch criteria doc. If A looks feasible and safe, we launch pilot next sprint.

raj: Also: set a hard bar — if we can't meet p99 targets in spike, escalate to B and justify Private roadmap priority for these accounts.

olivia: Sounds good. I'll book a 30m sync Friday 10am to review spike results. Thanks all :thumbsup:
